text:
To: All Employees
From: Imogen Hart, Director of Human Resources
Subject: Parental leave

Following consultation with employee representatives, the company's parental leave policy will be [1] with effect from 1 April. [2] The enhanced rate, which replaces the previous statutory minimum, will apply to all employees who have completed twelve months' service by the expected date of birth.

[3], the period of leave will be extended from twenty-six to thirty-nine weeks, [4] employees may take on a part-time basis. Further details, including a worked example of the calculation, are available on the intranet.

questions.explanation: A policy that changes 'with effect from 1 April' is 'revised'; 'revived' means brought back, 'revoked' means canceled, and 'revolved' does not fit.

choices: Pay during the first sixteen weeks of leave will remain at the statutory minimum for all employees concerned.
Pay during the first sixteen weeks of leave will be raised to the full salary of the employee concerned.
Pay during the final sixteen weeks of leave will be reduced to half the salary of the employee concerned.
Leave during the first sixteen weeks will be available to the employee on request, subject to approval.
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to 'The enhanced rate', so the previous one must announce a higher rate of pay; only the first does.
The sentence adds a second improvement to the first; the others mark contrast or consequence.
'Which' refers to the leave and is the object of 'may take'.
